headline: Highest risk is medium: shared file-based workflows and MCP/tooling create prompt-injection and data-leakage pathways, while direct capability conflict is limited by caveman’s no-egress profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman uses MCP and reads/writes project files like CLAUDE.md, while marketingskills references shared skill/context files and multiple agent surfaces. That creates a plausible file- or MCP-mediated injection path in default workflows. The pair is not directly documented interacting, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or skill directory, injected instructions can cross from one to the other.
IF either agent treats file contents as trusted instructions, prompt injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories.
Disable shared MCP endpoints for the pair.
Add a provenance header check before consuming file content.
Review CLAUDE.md and skill files for untrusted text.
requires-engineering: enforce read-only ingestion for cross-agent artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while marketingskills reads and writes skill/context files and has allowlisted network egress. If they share a workspace, sensitive content from caveman can flow into marketingskills outputs or uploads. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF the two agents share a filesystem or synced workspace, caveman logs can be read by marketingskills.
IF marketingskills sends workspace-derived content to its allowlisted endpoints, leaked notes can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Keep caveman logs in a separate directory.
Restrict marketingskills to sanitized inputs only.
Rotate or redact session logs before sharing files.
Audit which files are uploaded or summarized.
requires-engineering: add per-agent workspace isolation and DLP controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: marketingskills can read and write files and spawn subprocesses, but caveman is documented with network_egress none and no write or subprocess capability is shown. Overlap is therefore limited and the main conflict risk is only if an external orchestrator places both on the same mutable files. That makes the blast radius small and the pathway configuration-dependent.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF an orchestrator launches concurrent runs against shared state, race conditions become possible.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Run only one writer at a time.
Use file locks for shared artifacts.
Keep caveman read-only where possible.
requires-engineering: add concurrency control around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman produces content-writing outputs and marketingskills is a marketing agent that can act on files and subprocesses. If marketingskills consumes caveman output as authoritative copy, errors can cascade into published marketing material. There is no evidence of built-in verification between them, so the default risk is a medium-quality propagation path.
conditions: IF marketingskills uses caveman text without a review step, hallucinations can be propagated.
IF downstream publishing or file writes are automated, the error can reach external artifacts.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before publication.
Require source citations for factual claims.
Compare outputs against a checklist.
Limit caveman to draft-only generation.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking before write actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, and neither profile states regulated data handling or residency commitments. caveman touches session logs and memory files, while marketingskills touches marketing context, but no explicit compliance mismatch is documented. Because the relevant residency/retention facts are absent, the safest supported verdict is low rather than none.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into caveman session logs, retention policy review becomes necessary.
IF marketing context includes personal data and is shared across tools, local policy alignment is required.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared files.
Document retention for logs and marketing context.
Redact personal data before handoff.
Confirm storage location for each agent.
requires-engineering: publish a formal data-processing and retention policy.
